newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SOME FREE MARKET COMPANIES COULD FACE SUSPENSION.
newsitem.headline: SOME FREE MARKET COMPANIES COULD FACE SUSPENSION.

text.p: The Tallinn stock exchange said on Wednesday that it will suspend any free market listed company on June 6 that fails to meet its new information requirements.

"The listing committee decided last night that it will suspend companies on June 6 if they have not complied with the new free market information requirements," Helo Meigas, managing director of the Estonian bourse, told Reuters.
"The June 6 date gives the companies time to comply," she added.
Meigas declined to name those companies who have yet to provide all the necessary information, saying that they are reviewing what information has already been sent to the bourse.

The Estonian stock exchange decided in April to tighten free market regulations, and now requires all companies on the list to publish their financial results four times a year and to notify the bourse of any major changes to their activities.
